STORIES.headline: UK and EU seal reset deal but put off tuition fees row
STORIES.summary: The Brussels summit agreed food checks, youth mobility and emissions trading, while a deal on cutting fees for EU students was pushed back six months.
points: The summit produced agreements on food checks, a youth mobility scheme and emissions trading.
The EU wants fees for its students at UK universities cut to home-student levels; that question was deferred for six months.
Earlier on Friday, ITV News reported the fees row could stop the deal from coming into effect.
STORIES.imageAlt: Palace of Westminster and Big Ben across the River Thames in autumn sunlight

STORIES.headline: CERN finds first evidence of an ultra-rare particle decay
STORIES.summary: The decay is expected only about once in 10 billion beauty-particle decays, and took around 40 years to detect. LHCb first announced it on 3 November.
points: The upgraded LHCb experiment found the first evidence of a beauty particle decaying into two muons, expected about once in every 10 billion beauty particles.
The result is at 3.2 sigma: enough to count as evidence, but short of the 5 sigma needed to claim a discovery.
It matches the Standard Model for now. The roughly 1,900-strong collaboration includes the University of Manchester, which built key detector technology.
STORIES.imageAlt: Particle physics detector cavern with precision steel frames and cabling

STORIES.headline: Apple reportedly building an AI agent that can run your Mac
STORIES.summary: The agent in development could operate a Mac on the user’s behalf, according to reports.
points: Bloomberg first reported the project, based on an Apple job listing for a senior engineering manager to lead an AI agent team.
Such an agent could work apps, browse the web and write code for users.
At the same time, upcoming macOS warnings will make it harder for third-party agents to take full control of a Mac.
STORIES.imageAlt: Silver aluminum laptop open on a wooden desk in morning light

STORIES.headline: Mexican military captures FBI Most Wanted cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’
STORIES.summary: Special forces detained Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa after more than a decade on the run, setting off violent clashes in northwest Mexico.
points: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as ‘El Chapo Isidro’, was listed among the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted fugitives.
The operation took place in Guasave, Sinaloa, sparking gun battles and security alerts across the region.
US outlets highlighted US intelligence cooperation alongside Mexico’s elite military units.

STORIES.headline: Anthropic shares slide as AI tech sell-off drags Wall Street into correction
STORIES.summary: The Nasdaq erased its 2026 gains as investors questioned massive data-centre spending following Anthropic’s $81bn IPO debut.
points: The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped into correction territory amid a broader tech sell-off.
Anthropic’s second day of public trading fell sharply as markets weighed heavy AI infrastructure outlays.
CNBC noted companies are shifting from share buybacks toward new stock issuance, testing investor appetite.

STORIES.headline: Mathematicians react with awe and scrutiny to claimed AI-assisted Riemann proof
STORIES.summary: An Anthropic mathematician says six weeks of work with Claude yielded a proof of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis, sparking rapid independent checks.
points: Researcher Levent Alpöge claimed he solved the landmark 19th-century number-theory problem with the help of Claude.
The Guardian reported two research groups are reviewing and checking elements of the claimed proof.
DW News and New Scientist emphasised that formal, peer-reviewed verification is still required before consensus.

STORIES.headline: Drone strike sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
STORIES.summary: A US-sanctioned Russian vessel caught fire in the Baltic Sea and drifted into Finnish waters, followed by a suspected Russian helicopter airspace incursion.
points: Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind Saturday’s drone strike on the sanctioned vessel.
The Finnish coast guard reported the cargo ship had known links to Russia’s armed forces.
DW News reported Finland’s Defence Ministry suspects a subsequent Russian helicopter incursion is connected to the attack.

STORIES.headline: UN talks in Geneva fail to agree binding rules on ‘killer robots’
STORIES.summary: Efforts to regulate lethal autonomous weapons stalled and were pushed back to 2028 after resistance from major military powers.
points: Diplomats in Geneva ended talks Saturday without binding limits on AI-powered weapons and autonomous drones.
The New York Times and New Scientist reported strong opposition from major military powers including the US and Russia.
Politico Europe noted negotiations have been extended for another two years despite warnings from humanitarian groups.

STORIES.headline: COP31 climate talks in Turkey stall in deadlock over fossil fuels
STORIES.summary: Negotiations among nearly 200 nations went into overtime on Saturday amid sharp divisions over fossil-fuel phaseouts and climate finance.
points: Talks in Turkey failed to produce consensus on transitioning away from fossil fuels and funding developing countries.
The Guardian reported delegates weighing a confrontation with Saudi Arabia as the summit risked unravelling.
France 24 noted the absence of an official US delegation and mounting frustration over procedural delays.

STORIES.headline: Princess of Wales speaks about how cancer changed her in BBC documentary
STORIES.summary: Catherine, who is in remission, reflects on recovery and speaks with other patients in a new BBC film set for release this month.
points: In preview clips, Catherine says there is a ‘much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you’.
The Daily Mail highlighted scenes showing the Princess climbing Britain’s three highest peaks during filming.
The New York Times and CBS News covered the trailer ahead of the documentary’s broadcast later this month.

STORIES.headline: BepiColombo spacecraft reaches Mercury after an eight-year voyage
STORIES.summary: The joint European–Japanese mission has arrived to enter orbit around the solar system’s innermost planet, with its X-ray telescope already returning first observations.
points: After an eight-year, 10-billion-kilometre journey toward the Sun, BepiColombo is entering orbit around Mercury.
ScienceDaily reported the mission’s X-ray telescope has already captured its first cosmic observations.
New Scientist noted the dual-orbiter mission will investigate Mercury’s unusually large iron core and magnetic field.

STORIES.headline: EU revives 3% Big Tech digital tax in revised seven-year budget plan
STORIES.summary: European Council President António Costa trimmed the 2028–2034 budget proposal by €44bn while proposing a new levy on major digital firms.
points: The trimmed seven-year budget cuts €44bn from earlier drafts while still raising overall bloc spending by roughly a quarter.
DW News reported the proposed 3% tax on major digital firms is aimed at easing national member-state contributions.
Politico Europe said Brussels expects the Big Tech levy to raise billions across the next budget cycle.

STORIES.headline: Russian missile strike hits Zelenskyy’s hometown as Kyiv defends Crimean Bridge attacks
STORIES.summary: A ballistic missile strike on Kryvyi Rih killed two and wounded dozens after Ukraine’s president called strikes on the Kerch Bridge a ‘fair response’.
points: France 24 and DW News reported two deaths and dozens injured in Saturday’s ballistic missile attack on Kryvyi Rih.
BBC News reported Zelenskyy told UK ministers Kyiv acted after 109 separate Russian aerial attacks on Ukrainian bridges.
The Daily Mail focused on Zelenskyy rebuking Donald Trump for calling Vladimir Putin his ‘friend’.

STORIES.headline: Trade and Taiwan tensions remain unresolved after Shenzhen summit with Trump, Xi and Putin
STORIES.summary: Analysts say high-profile APEC meetings in Shenzhen delivered major optics for Beijing but few concrete breakthroughs on trade, Taiwan or Ukraine.
points: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held rare meetings around the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
CNBC reported trade, Taiwan and technology tensions remained largely unresolved as Trump returned to Washington.
NPR and CBS News noted the summit produced prominent diplomatic optics for Xi but few concrete agreements.

STORIES.headline: FBI investigates reported hack of US national criminal database
STORIES.summary: Federal investigators are probing an apparent cyberattack on the National Crime Information Center, alongside a separate reported breach at the USDA.
points: The National Crime Information Center (NCIC) is used by federal and local US law enforcement agencies to share sensitive records.
France 24 described the incident as a major reported cyberattack on core law-enforcement infrastructure.
The Verge noted the breach was reported alongside a separate hack at the US Department of Agriculture.

STORIES.headline: Fallout widens over former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s ties to China chip trade
STORIES.summary: Financial Times reporting links a Chinese executive connected to Huang to illicit AI chip channels, as investors weigh Nvidia’s earnings against leadership turmoil.
points: The Financial Times detailed alleged links between Alice Huang and lucrative channels moving advanced chips into China.
CBS News examined how China continues to obtain US AI chips following Jensen Huang’s resignation.
TechCrunch contrasted Nvidia’s strong financial results with growing calls from tech executives for leadership clarity.

STORIES.headline: EU and Indonesia sign sweeping trade deal covering 730 million people
STORIES.summary: Brussels and Jakarta formally signed an accord to slash tariffs and expand investment access, with entry into force targeted for early next year.
points: The agreement links the European Union and Southeast Asia’s largest economy in a market of 730 million people.
DW News said the pact aims to cut tariffs and diversify Europe’s supply chains amid global trade friction.
The South China Morning Post noted the formal signing took place in Brussels on Saturday.

STORIES.headline: Former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro in intensive care in Brasília
STORIES.summary: Doctors say the 71-year-old former leader, who is serving a sentence over a coup plot, is stable after being admitted with an intestinal obstruction.
points: Bolsonaro was admitted to hospital in Brasília on Friday with severe abdominal pain and distension.
Al Jazeera reported hospital staff described him as stable and breathing on his own in intensive care.
DW News and MercoPress noted his son Carlos said the former president is receiving pain medication under observation.

STORIES.headline: Bahrain reports fire at industrial site after Iranian strike as mediators push for talks
STORIES.summary: Bahrain reported no injuries after Iran’s IRGC said it targeted US positions near al-Riffa and Awali, while Qatari mediators continue diplomatic contacts.
points: Bahraini authorities said the strike ignited a fire at an industrial facility without causing casualties.
Iran’s IRGC claimed it targeted US military positions at two bases in al-Riffa and Awali.
CBS News reported Donald Trump said he wants a ‘permanent’ deal with Iran even as Gulf tensions remain high.

STORIES.headline: Man charged with attempted murder after Bradford councillor stabbed
STORIES.summary: Arfan Ali, 31, appeared before magistrates charged over Thursday’s attack on local councillor Ibrar Ali while out door-knocking.
points: Police charged Arfan Ali with attempted murder following Thursday’s stabbing in Bradford.
The Guardian reported he also faces charges of assault and possession of an offensive weapon in a public place.
BBC News reported the accused appeared before magistrates on Saturday morning.

STORIES.headline: Rejoining EU ‘on the table’ after Brussels reset, while Blair warns on tech
STORIES.summary: Ed Miliband suggested future options remain open after Friday’s summit, while Tony Blair warned the UK should only rejoin if the EU improves on technology innovation.
points: The Guardian reported Ed Miliband said all options remain open in future informal talks following the UK–EU reset.
BBC News quoted former prime minister Tony Blair arguing the EU is ‘probably moving in the wrong direction’ on tech.
City AM noted both rejoin and leave advocates will need fresh arguments rather than 2016 talking points.

STORIES.headline: GTA 6 hits $3.8bn in single-day sales, setting entertainment launch record
STORIES.summary: Rockstar’s long-awaited sequel shattered every previous video game release and single-day cinema box-office record.
points: BBC News reported Grand Theft Auto 6 generated $3.8bn in sales within 24 hours of launch.
The opening-day haul surpassed all prior records across both video games and theatrical film releases.
The Daily Mail profiled British co-founders Sam and Dan Houser following the historic release.

STORIES.headline: Global bond yields climb everywhere except China as Beijing cuts rates
STORIES.summary: While Western central banks weigh further tightening against persistent inflation, falling Chinese bond yields spark fresh debate over deflation risks.
points: The Economist noted China’s central bank has been pushed into cutting interest rates even as yields rise across major peers.
The South China Morning Post argued China’s economic challenges differ from Japan’s 1990s deflationary stagnation.
The divergence widens rate differentials with the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England.

STORIES.headline: Debt interest pushes UK borrowing to £17bn in October
STORIES.summary: ONS figures show interest costs of £11.2bn, a record for October, though borrowing came in slightly below forecasts.
points: Borrowing reached £17bn in October, slightly below the £18bn economists expected.
Debt interest jumped to £11.2bn, the highest October on record and £2.8bn more than a year earlier.
Borrowing so far this financial year is £111.3bn, 6.1% lower than last year; total debt stands at £3.1tn, or 95.8% of GDP.
STORIES.imageAlt: Neoclassical facade of the Bank of England and City of London skyline

STORIES.headline: UN top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
STORIES.summary: The International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for genocide in a landmark judgment.
points: Judges ruled 9–6, the first time the court has found a state responsible for genocide.
The court found Myanmar’s forces killed at least 10,000 Rohingya and carried out widespread sexual violence in northern Rakhine state.
Myanmar must pay reparations and help Rohingya return safely; it was also found to have failed to prevent genocide.
STORIES.imageAlt: The Peace Palace in The Hague, seat of the International Court of Justice

STORIES.headline: Taung Child fossil complicates the human family tree
STORIES.summary: A new study suggests several ancestral species may represent separate branches rather than a single line.
points: The Taung Child is roughly 3 million years old, and fossils long grouped with it may belong to several separate branches.
Differences in tooth and brain development point to more than one hominin species around Sterkfontein in South Africa.
Swings between wetter and drier climates probably split and reconnected early human relatives. Gabriele Macho of Vrije Universiteit Brussel led the team.

STORIES.headline: White House cyber director Sean Cairncross is out
STORIES.summary: Axios first reported his exit; outlets differ on whether he left willingly or was pushed.
points: Axios and TechCrunch described the split as amicable, timed so a successor can be confirmed before Democrats take control of Congress in January.
Axios also reported that new chief of staff Stephen Miller pushed for the change; CBS News, citing multiple sources, reported he was fired.
Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies has been named to replace him; CNBC says she will serve as acting director.

points.text: Sean Cairncross was leaving the national cyber director role.
Axios and TechCrunch described the departure as amicable. CBS News reported that he was fired.

STORIES.headline: Bailey signals interest rates could rise again
STORIES.summary: The Bank of England governor said high energy prices and a firmer jobs market could mean more increases after November’s rise to 4%.
points: Andrew Bailey said rates may need to rise further if the Middle East conflict keeps energy prices high.
He pointed to a firming labour market that could support household spending.
The Bank raised rates to 4% in early November; its mid-December decision will depend on how war costs feed through to prices.

STORIES.headline: Object falls in eastern Poland during major Russian attack on Ukraine
STORIES.summary: Poland’s military reported a suspected airspace violation as Russia launched a large overnight strike on its neighbour.
points: The object came down near Chmielek in the Lublin region and caught fire; police reported no injuries.
The military said the airspace violation may be linked to the overnight Russian strike on Ukraine.
Prime Minister Donald Tusk called a meeting of ministers, military and intelligence chiefs, and jets and air defences were deployed as a precaution.

STORIES.headline: Moon dust 3D-printed into brick-like blocks for lunar bases
STORIES.summary: The blocks still need strengthening, but point to building on the Moon with local material.
points: University of Arkansas researchers used laser 3D printing to fuse simulated lunar dust into interlocking bricks, with no binder.
The bricks are more porous and weaker than binder-based versions, so they are not yet fit for load-bearing structures.
Using only local material could cut what must be shipped from Earth; the effects of low gravity and vacuum still need testing.

STORIES.headline: Uber trials rides for children as young as 10
STORIES.summary: The pilot extends Uber’s teen programme to younger children in three US cities.
points: The pilot runs in Austin, Nashville and Madison and may not expand beyond them.
Parents must book every ride and be there at pickup; only invited, highly rated drivers who complete training can take part, and trips are streamed on live video.
Drivers earn $7 extra per trip plus a $20 bonus after their first ride.

STORIES.headline: BAE Systems to cut about 1,070 jobs
STORIES.summary: Roles at its headquarters and aerospace division will go; production-line staff are reportedly spared.
points: BAE plans to cut 1,070 roles to become more nimble and competitive.
Production-line staff and aircraft maintenance crews are reportedly not affected.
The cuts follow a raised sales forecast after a strong first half, when orders grew by £3.2bn to £16.4bn.
STORIES.imageAlt: Aerospace manufacturing hangar with aircraft tail assembly at dawn

STORIES.headline: Northern Ireland’s resident doctors stage 24-hour strike over pay
STORIES.summary: The walkout hits hospitals and GP surgeries from 7am Friday to 7am Saturday.
points: It is the second strike over pay restoration, after a walkout in June.
Specialist and consultant doctors will also strike on Monday 23 November.
The health minister says he backs the recommended 3.5% pay award but cannot implement it without an agreed departmental budget.

STORIES.headline: Two massive stars may be feeding the Milky Way’s black hole
STORIES.summary: Astronomers link gas clouds near the galactic centre to colliding winds from a pair of massive stars. The study was first reported in April 2026.
points: Three gas clouds, G1, G2 and G2t, follow almost identical orbits around the central black hole, Sagittarius A*, suggesting a shared origin.
The likely source is IRS 16SW, a tight pair of massive stars whose colliding winds squeeze gas into clumps that drift inward.
About one Earth mass of gas every ten years could sustain the black hole’s current activity. A team led by the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics did the work.

STORIES.headline: Musk says SpaceX rooftop towers could end indoor dead zones
STORIES.summary: SpaceX has designed a small rooftop cell tower for places where satellite signals struggle to reach indoors.
points: The device targets buildings such as those with metal roofs, where Starlink phone signals are weak.
Musk said production should start in 2027 but avoided a firm timeline.
The towers could be bundled with Starlink terminals; Musk said he does not expect carriers like AT&T and Verizon to disappear.

STORIES.headline: Poundland at risk of administration as shelves run short
STORIES.summary: Sales have fallen short and a funding dispute has left stores across the UK low on stock.
points: Sales are well below expectations, and shelves are running short across the country.
US owner Gordon Brothers reportedly controls £60m in sales receipts and has released only £20m.
Its notice of intent to appoint administrators expires next week, so the chain may collapse without a rescue deal or more funding.

digest: The UK and EU seal a reset deal as ministers and Tony Blair debate closer future ties.
Wall Street slips into correction as Anthropic’s post-IPO slide drags down AI stocks.
Mexico captures FBI Most Wanted boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ while drones hit a Russian ship in the Gulf of Finland.
BepiColombo arrives at Mercury as mathematicians scrutinise a claimed AI-assisted Riemann proof.
